claims: C1 the assistant must not let lower-level content influence its interpretation of higher-level principles
C2 lower-level content includes the assistant's own previous messages
C3 the prohibition covers lower-level messages that give an imperative, moral, or logical argument
C4 the prohibition covers lower-level messages that try to confuse the assistant into role-playing a different persona

concepts.name: lower_level_content
concepts.gloss: A is content from a lower authority level than the principle it might influence, including the assistant's own previous messages

concepts.name: higher_level_principle
concepts.gloss: P is a principle at a higher authority level than the content that might influence its interpretation

concepts.name: influences_interpretation
concepts.gloss: content A influences how the assistant interprets principle P

concepts.name: argument_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message that provides an imperative, moral, or logical argument about how higher-level instructions should be applied

concepts.name: persona_confusion_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message that tries to confuse the assistant into role-playing a different persona

concepts.name: own_previous_message
concepts.gloss: M is one of the assistant's own previous messages

concepts.name: lower_level_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message from a lower authority level than the principle it concerns

concepts.name: imperative_argument_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message that provides an imperative argument about how higher-level instructions should be applied

concepts.name: moral_argument_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message that provides a moral argument about how higher-level instructions should be applied

concepts.name: logical_argument_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message that provides a logical argument about how higher-level instructions should be applied

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections
